title: LORA Tunnel SD configuration, schema 1
description: Save as /lora-tunnel/config.json on SD. Current firmware accepts a 16 KiB file and fixed 16 KiB JSON arena; additional fields are retained but not necessarily implemented.

enabled.description: Fresh installations keep LoRa off until an explicit region selection. This firmware only receives; it never transmits.

selection_complete.description: An explicit Skip saves true with region UNSET, completing first setup while leaving LoRa disabled. Supported named regions and valid legacy US configurations also count as a completed choice.

region.description: Omitted on legacy schema-1 files: enabled or explicit-frequency configs retain previous US settings; a bare disabled config remains UNSET. 433/470 MHz profiles require other hardware. Firmware validates occupied bandwidth against the target: Heltec 863-928 MHz or Cardputer U214 868-923 MHz.

name.description: Firmware limit is 39 UTF-8 bytes, not arbitrary Unicode characters.

frequency_mhz.description: UNSET uses zero. A named region defaults to its LongFast center when omitted; firmware also requires the full selected bandwidth to fit that region. Legacy configs without region remain limited to 902-928 MHz.

categories.description: Omitted means every category; an empty list disables all Recon categories. These are evidence categories, not authenticated device identities.

buttons_enabled.description: Enable the physical-button shortcuts; Cardputer keyboard and Heltec touchscreen controls remain available.

uploads.description: Explicit opt-in per service. Only closed Wardriver sessions are eligible while capture is stopped and configured home Wi-Fi is available. Never automatically pauses capture.

credentials.description: Private SD plaintext settings, masked in UI. Automatic sending requires the corresponding uploads switch. Never include real values in examples/logs/source control.

credential.description: Firmware capacity is 127 UTF-8 bytes plus NUL, not 127 arbitrary Unicode characters. Empty string means unconfigured.
